expected_level_description: You can: - manage configuration items and related information - manage service compliance and risk

You can: - lead investigative work into problems and opportunities in existing processes - lead the collection of information and creation of recommendations for improvements - absorb large amounts of conflicting information and use it to produce solutions

You can: - analyse current processes, and identify and implement opportunities to optimise them - lead and develop a team of experts to deliver service improvements - help to evaluate and establish requirements for the implementation of changes by setting policy and standards
You can: - use data analytics skills to make decisions that enhance business performance
You can: - take accountability for issues that occur and be proactive in searching for potential problems - achieve excellent user outcomes
You can: - see the bigger picture by taking groups of services and investigating how to get the best of underlying services
You can: - show you have an expert certificate in the service management framework qualification

You can: - negotiate with and influence stakeholders, and manage relationships effectively - influence decisions, deal with challenging situations and remove blockers - build long-term strategic relationships and communicate clearly and regularly with stakeholders, supporting mutual needs and commitments while focusing on user needs

You can: - define strategies and policies, providing guidance to others on working in the strategic context - evaluate current strategies to ensure business requirements are being met and exceeded where possible
You can: - understand the core technical concepts related to the role, and apply them with guidance

You can: - collaborate with user researchers and can represent users internally - explain the difference between user needs and the desires of the user - champion user research to focus on all users - prioritise and define approaches to understand the user story, guiding others in doing so - offer recommendations on the best tools and methods to use

You can: - analyse how a service fits into care pathways across organisations - work with clinicians, care staff, and patients to shape digital services - explain the effect of digital decisions on care, safety, and staff workload
You can: - apply data protection principles to your work - contribute to data protection impact assessments - handle information requests and records correctly
You can: - take part in hazard workshops and contribute to a hazard log - follow the clinical risk management process for your work - provide evidence for a clinical safety case, such as test results
You can: - run the risk process for a directorate or programme - assess risks against the risk appetite and escalate them - report on risks to committees
You can: - supervise day-to-day work and give feedback - take part in recruitment and induction - hold regular one-to-one conversations
You can: - follow the rules for spending and ordering - explain how your work is funded
